querysurge.ruleBasedChecks: FAQ lists 'field-level rules (nulls, domains, formats)' and running 'data quality rules'; the features page itself is comparison-centric (QueryPairs, duplicate row checking, column thresholds).

datagaps-etl-validator.ruleBasedChecks: ETL testing guide: detects 'unexpected null values in required fields', unexpected duplicate records, and 'Verifies business logic with SQL, Python or Scala'. Range checks not named.
datagaps-etl-validator.alerts: Validation results can be sent to 'Email, Teams, Slack, and Jira'.
datagaps-etl-validator.cloudWarehouses: Lists Snowflake, Databricks, Redshift, Azure Synapse, Microsoft Fabric, Google BigQuery.

rightdata-datatrust.flatFiles: No CSV/JSON/Parquet mention on DataTrust pages; the FAQ says connector support must be confirmed per source.
rightdata-datatrust.noCodeTests: Vendor llms-full.txt lists 'Zero-code rule creation with AI-recommended quality rules' as a DataTrust capability.
rightdata-datatrust.scheduling: Product page Job Designer caption: 'scheduled FDR, validation, TDR, and email steps'.

tricentis-data-integrity.ruleBasedChecks: Rules cheat sheet: 'Correctness: Uniqueness, not null, Hash-Comparisons, Data Ranges'; product page: validate data 'against business rules'.
tricentis-data-integrity.cicdIntegration: Snowflake testing page: 'Integrates into CI/CD pipelines'. Failing the build is not described explicitly.
tricentis-data-integrity.cloudWarehouses: Product page pre-built connectors: 'SAP, Salesforce, Oracle, SQL Server, Snowflake, Databricks, and more'; the data warehouse testing guide also names BigQuery. Tosca docs connect through ODBC.
tricentis-data-integrity.alerts: Only profiling that can 'alert you to any values that fall out of the norm' and generic advice; no email/Slack/Teams channel documented.
tricentis-data-integrity.noCodeTests: UNCERTAIN: learn page says tests are 'scriptless' (model-based); product page says 'Low-code test authoring' without deep coding expertise.

bigeval.alerts: Docs: BiG EVAL 'can send you eMail alerts'; Slack/Teams via Power Automate, webhooks or scripts.
bigeval.flatFiles: Docs: 'Textfile' datasource type connects directly to CSV files (Excel also). Parquet/JSON not documented.
bigeval.cloudWarehouses: Only Snowflake is named (gallery tag); Databricks and BigQuery are not documented.
bigeval.noCodeTests: First-testcase tutorial requires entering a SQL query into the probe; no no-code builder documented.

datafold.ruleBasedChecks: Data Test monitors: standard tests for non-null, unique, numeric ranges, accepted values, referential integrity, plus custom SQL.
datafold.flatFiles: Data diff API file sources support csv, excel and parquet (s3://, gs://, abfss://, https://).
datafold.alerts: Monitor notifications: email, Slack, Microsoft Teams, PagerDuty, webhooks.

informatica-cloud-data-validation.ruleBasedChecks: Docs describe only comparing two data sets (source vs target, full or aggregate); no single-table rule checks documented.
informatica-cloud-data-validation.cicdIntegration: A REST API can run test cases and suites and return results, but no CI/CD pipeline integration is described.
informatica-cloud-data-validation.flatFiles: Supported connections include 'Flat file'; Amazon S3 v2 supports flat files and Parquet; ADLS Gen2 lists 'CSV flat file'.

dbt.ruleBasedChecks: Generic tests unique, not_null, accepted_values, relationships plus singular SQL tests.
dbt.flatFiles: Tests run as SQL in the data platform; CSVs only via seeds, which dbt loads into the warehouse first.
dbt.alerts: Job notifications by email, Slack and Microsoft Teams, including on failure.
dbt.sourceTargetCompare: INTERPRETATION: Advanced CI 'compare changes' (Enterprise, Enterprise+) shows row/column differences between the CI build and production models; both must be on the same connection. No cross-system source-to-target comparison.
dbt.noCodeTests: Tests are defined in .yml/.sql files; Canvas (visual editor) is no longer sold to new accounts from 2026-11-12 and its docs do not mention tests.

tools.name: DataKitchen DataOps TestGen
tools.tagline: Open-source data quality testing that profiles your tables and generates tests for you.
tools.bestFor: Teams that want auto-generated data quality tests on warehouse tables and files without writing YAML
tools.description: TestGen profiles tables and generates data quality tests from the profile, with 34 auto-generated test types and 19 business-rule and custom SQL test types. It runs tests on a schedule as SQL inside the database, works with 14 databases including Snowflake, Databricks SQL and BigQuery, and also reads CSV, Parquet and JSON files. The open-source edition is Apache 2.0 and free for 1 user, 1 connection and 1 project; Enterprise costs $100 per month per user and per database connection.
pros: Free Apache 2.0 edition with unlimited tables and data volume
Generates tests from profiling: 34 auto-generated test types plus 19 business-rule and custom SQL types
Reads CSV, Parquet and JSON files from a local path, Amazon S3 or Azure Blob Storage
Alerts by email, Slack or Microsoft Teams, plus scheduled runs
REST API and MCP server for automation from pipelines and AI assistants
cons: Open-source edition is limited to 1 user, 1 connection and 1 project
Enterprise is priced per user and per connection: 10 users and 3 connections cost $1,300 per month
Self-hosted only; the docs say TestGen runs inside your network and mention no hosted SaaS
The testgen CLI is deprecated; CI/CD use goes through the REST API
No self-serve Enterprise trial; evaluations are arranged through sales
tools.freePlanDetails: Open Source edition, $0 'free forever': 1 user, 1 connection, 1 project, core test types and profiling, unlimited tables and data volume, community support.

priceUnit.long: per user and per database connection, per month

tools.name: Recce
tools.tagline: Data review agent that diffs dbt changes against production in every pull request.
tools.bestFor: dbt teams that want data diffs and review checklists on every pull request
tools.description: Recce compares a pull request's dbt environment with production and reports row count, profile, value, Top-K, histogram and custom query diffs, plus lineage impact. Recce Cloud runs this automatically from GitHub Actions or GitLab CI on Snowflake, Databricks, BigQuery and Redshift, and the open-source toolkit is Apache 2.0. The Free cloud plan is $0 and the Team plan is $300 per month, or $250 per month billed annually, with unlimited seats.
pros: Row-level value diffs keyed on primary keys, plus profile, Top-K, histogram and query diffs
CI setup for GitHub Actions and GitLab CI; the Free plan includes automated CI validation, PR comments and PR blocking
Team plan is a flat price with unlimited seats
Preset checks can be added from the Recce Cloud UI instead of editing recce.yml
Open-source toolkit under Apache 2.0
cons: Built around dbt; Recce Cloud supports only Snowflake, Databricks, BigQuery and Redshift
Compares base and PR environments in one warehouse, not a source system against a target system
No scheduled runs or failure alerts documented; validation is triggered by pull requests
Free plan caps preset checks at 10 and agent reviews at 100 per month; Team allows 1,000 agent reviews
No assertion tests of its own; not-null and unique appear only as profile statistics
tools.freePlanDetails: Free cloud plan, $0: 10 customized preset checks, 100 agent reviews per month, automated CI validation and PR comments, PR blocking, community support. The open-source toolkit is also free (Apache 2.0).

plans.notes: Apache 2.0 toolkit (pip install recce); runs locally; checks run manually or with recce run.

plans.notes: Recce Cloud. 10 customized preset checks, 100 agent reviews/month, CI validation, PR comments, PR blocking.

plans.notes: $300/month on monthly billing; $250/month when paid annually. Unlimited preset checks, 1,000 agent reviews/month, shared team checklists, unlimited seats, 48-hour email support SLA.

plans.notes: Custom limits and volume pricing, SSO, BYOC, RBAC, dedicated support with custom SLAs, analytics dashboard, semantic layer support.

tools.name: SQLMesh
tools.tagline: Open-source SQL transformation framework with built-in audits, unit tests and table diffs.
tools.bestFor: Data teams building SQL pipelines who want tests, audits and diffs inside the transformation framework
tools.description: SQLMesh is an Apache 2.0 data transformation framework with 29 built-in audits such as not_null, unique_values and accepted_range, custom SQL audits, unit tests and a table_diff command for row-level comparisons. It was built by Tobiko Data, which Fivetran acquired in 2025, and Fivetran contributed the project to the Linux Foundation on March 25, 2026. Tobiko Cloud, the commercial edition, is sold on quote with a platform fee plus a pay-as-you-go consumption fee.
pros: 29 built-in audits plus custom SQL audits; blocking audits halt a plan or run
Unit tests (sqlmesh test) and row-level table diffs between environments or two tables
GitHub Actions CI/CD bot runs unit tests and the linter on pull requests and updates check runs
Notifications to Slack (webhook or API) and email (SMTP) on audit failures and run failures
Free under Apache 2.0, governed by the Linux Foundation, with 16 execution engines
cons: Tests are tied to SQLMesh models; it is not a standalone tester for pipelines built with other tools
Cross-database table diffing is a Tobiko Cloud feature
Tobiko Cloud prices are not published
GitHub Actions is the only CI bot documented
Audits and tests are written as SQL and YAML; the open-source tool has no visual test builder
tools.freePlanDetails: SQLMesh is free and open source (Apache 2.0) under the Linux Foundation.

plans.name: Tobiko Cloud
plans.notes: Platform fee plus pay-as-you-go consumption fee; no seat or project limits; contact sales. Cloud-only, hybrid (self-hosted runners) or fully on-premise. Adds observability, built-in scheduling and cross-database table diff.

tools.integrations: Engines: Athena, Azure SQL, BigQuery, ClickHouse, Databricks, DuckDB, Fabric, MotherDuck, MSSQL, MySQL, Postgres, GCP Postgres, Redshift, Snowflake, Spark, Trino. Tools: dbt, dlt, GitHub Actions, Kestra. Notifications: Slack, SMTP email

tools.name: Pandera
tools.tagline: Open-source Python library for validating dataframes against schemas and checks.
tools.bestFor: Python data and ML engineers who want schema and value checks inside their code and tests
tools.description: Pandera is an MIT-licensed Union.ai open-source project for validating dataframe-like objects with schemas and checks such as nullable, unique, ranges, isin and custom functions. It supports pandas, polars, PySpark, Ibis, PyArrow and DataFusion backends, and the Ibis backend can reach BigQuery, Snowflake and Databricks. It is free; Union.ai sells its own platform but lists no paid Pandera edition.
pros: Free under the MIT license
Field-level checks: nullable, unique, gt/ge/le, in_range, isin, plus custom checks
Works with pandas, polars, PySpark, Ibis, PyArrow and DataFusion; Dask and Modin via the pandas backend
Ibis backend reaches BigQuery, Snowflake and Databricks
Schema inference and synthetic test data generation with Hypothesis
cons: Python code only; no UI for building tests
No built-in scheduler, alerting or source-to-target comparison
Ibis support is described as less mature than pandas support
Statistical hypothesis checks work only with the pandas backend
tools.freePlanDetails: Open source under the MIT license; install with pip.
